question: A cafe started with 44 customers. They added 74 (morning). They subtracted 100 for closing early (afternoon). They added 65 from evening opening. They added 20 more. They added 69 additional (evening surge). 'One distractor': the mall had 5000 visitors. After morning addition but before the subtraction, how many customers in the intermediate state?

A business had 158 dollars. They added 33 (morning). They subtracted 105 for initial cost. They multiplied by 4 for compound growth (afternoon). They divided by 4 for distribution (evening, using 'minutes to hours'). They subtracted 35 final expense. After addition/subtraction but before multiplication, how much in the morning state?

A business started with 226 dollars. They added 47 (morning). They multiplied by 9 through growth (afternoon). They subtracted 414 for overhead. They subtracted 751 for a major investment. They multiplied by 8 (evening). They multiplied by 9 for annual scaling. Using 'minutes to hours' and 'one distractor' (competitor earned 10000). After addition but before afternoon multiplication, how much?

A business had 209 dollars. They added 6 (morning). They subtracted 67 for costs (mid-morning). They multiplied by 7 through growth (afternoon). They multiplied by 2 for scaling. They added 26 from profit (evening). Using 'minutes to hours' as unit change and asking for intermediate state. After addition but before the cost subtraction, how much money?

A student had 157 dollars (morning). They subtracted 12 for supplies. They added 47 from work. They added 13 bonus (afternoon). They subtracted 37 for purchase. They added 26 back (from refund). They subtracted 97 for major expense. Using 'double' as a word quantity and 'one distractor' (a scholarship of 500 dollars). After supplies and work earnings but before bonus, how much in the intermediate?

A gym had 236 members (morning start). They multiplied by 6 for annual projection. They divided by 6 returning to original (mid-day adjustment). They divided by 4 for class grouping. They added 80 new members (afternoon). They added 51 more (evening). Showing morning/afternoon/evening progression and intermediate state. After multiplications and divisions but before adding new members, how many members?

A store had 50 items (starting inventory). They added 51 (morning restock). They subtracted 79 for sales (mid-morning). They added 32 from returns (afternoon). They multiplied by 8 for distribution projection (evening). Tom's store had 300 items separately (named comparison). After the additions and subtraction but before multiplication, how many items in the afternoon state?

A business started with 219 dollars. They subtracted 55 for overhead (morning). They multiplied by 4 through revenue (afternoon). They added 31 from profit (late afternoon). They added 78 more (early evening). They multiplied by 8 for annual projection. Using morning/afternoon/evening time structure. How much after overhead subtraction but before afternoon multiplication (intermediate)?

A student had 57 minutes of free time (morning start). They added 42 (morning activity). They subtracted 64 for work (mid-morning). They added 51 from free time (afternoon). They divided by half for class periods (evening). 'One distractor': class lasts 90 minutes but separate. Showing morning/afternoon/evening with intermediate questions. After subtraction but before adding afternoon time, how many minutes?

A project started with 12 tasks (morning). They added 23 (early morning work). They added 69 more (morning expansion). They multiplied by 7 for team assignment (afternoon). They multiplied by 4 for phase scaling (evening). Using 'minutes to hours' for task timing. Two team leaders (named but doesn't fit this problem). After both morning additions but before afternoon multiplication, how many tasks in the morning snapshot?

A factory started with 210 units. They multiplied by 6 (morning production). They multiplied by 5 more (morning continuation). They added 46 from supply (afternoon). They subtracted 2906 for major orders (evening). 'One distractor': annual capacity is 10000. Showing morning/afternoon/evening. After multiplications but before adding the supply, how many units in the morning state?

A business started with 192 dollars (morning base). They multiplied by 8 (morning growth). They multiplied by 7 (mid-morning scaling). They multiplied by 5 for projection (afternoon). They added 10 from refund (late afternoon). They subtracted 16943 for major investment (evening, using 'minutes to hours'). Tom and Sarah managed finances. After morning multiplications but before the afternoon multiplication, how much money?

A student had 170 points (morning tally). They added 59 (morning activity, afternoon update). They subtracted 13 (mid-afternoon). They subtracted 105 more (afternoon). They multiplied by 7 for semester projection (evening). Tom's score was 300 separately (named comparison). After additions and subtractions but before multiplication, how many points in the afternoon state?

A business had 226 dollars (morning). They added 22 (morning). They subtracted 211 for inventory (mid-morning). They multiplied by 8 for growth projection (afternoon). They subtracted 171 for operating cost. They multiplied by 8 more (evening). They added 29 final profit. Using 'double' as a word quantity and showing 'Tom and Sarah' as named managers. After addition but before first large subtraction, how much money in the late morning?

A student had 41 items (starting count). They doubled (multiplied by 2). They divided by half returning to original. They added 15 (morning). They added 60 (afternoon). They added 71 more (evening). They added 39 final items. Using 'double' as word quantity and 'Tom and Lisa' as named friends. After all operations—what was the total after adding 15 but before afternoon additions?

An athlete had 77 minutes of training (morning start). They multiplied by 9 (morning session). They subtracted 9 immediately after (mid-morning). They subtracted 461 for rest day (afternoon). They added 7 from bonus training (evening, using 'double' as word quantity). 'One distractor': full day is 1440 minutes. After multiplication and first subtraction but before the rest day subtraction, how many minutes in the afternoon?

A business had 199 dollars (starting). They doubled (multiplied by 2). They doubled again (multiplied by 2). They multiplied by 9 for growth. They divided by 4 for distribution. They subtracted 59 for expenses (evening). They added 5 from refund. Tom and Lisa managed it (named). After multiplications but before division, how much money in the morning?

A student had 197 dollars (morning state). They added 30 (morning). They subtracted 69 for books (mid-morning). They added 63 from work (afternoon). They added 8 bonus (late afternoon). They subtracted 50 for final cost (evening). Using 'minutes to hours' as unit change and 'Tom and Lisa' as named people. After first addition and subtraction but before work earnings, how much in the afternoon?

A library had 135 books (starting catalog). They divided by 3 for branch distribution (morning). They added 72 from donations (mid-morning). They subtracted 115 for archiving (afternoon). They added 6 final books (evening). Two managers tracked it (named: Manager A vs B). After division but before additions, how many books in the early morning state?

A manufacturing plant started with 143 items (morning production). They multiplied by 9 for batch calculation. They multiplied by 5 for shift scaling (afternoon). They subtracted 100 for quality control. They subtracted 2586 for inventory adjustment. They subtracted 3378 more. They multiplied by 4 for projections (evening). After multiplications but before quality control subtraction, how many units (intermediate state)?

A courier service started with 185 packages (morning load). They added 16 (morning addition). They added 58 more (mid-morning). They doubled (multiplied by 2, afternoon). They multiplied by 8 for route calculation. They multiplied by 4 for final scaling (evening). Using 'minutes to hours' to track delivery time. After additions but before doubling, how many packages in the mid-morning?

A baker had 46 loaves (morning production). They multiplied by 8 for batch size. They added 17 from supplier (mid-morning). They multiplied by 7 for delivery scaling (afternoon). They added 9 final orders (evening, using 'minutes to hours' for baking time). 'One distractor': oven capacity was 500 loaves. After multiplication but before supplier addition, how many loaves in the mid-morning?

A library had 134 books (morning inventory). They subtracted 108 for archiving (morning). They added 80 from donations (mid-morning). They added 66 more (afternoon). They multiplied by 3 for branch expansion. They subtracted 353 for redistribution (evening). 'One distractor': archive storage held 500 books. After subtraction and additions but before multiplication, how many books in the afternoon?

A bakery started with 54 items (morning start). They added 29 (morning). They doubled (multiplied by 2, morning/afternoon). They subtracted 28 for spoilage (mid-afternoon). They multiplied by 9 for batch calculation. They multiplied by 4 for scaling (evening, using 'double' as word quantity). 'One distractor': competitor made 500 items. After addition and doubling but before spoilage, how many items in the afternoon?

A factory started with 228 units (morning production). They divided by 4 for initial sorting (morning). They subtracted 41 defects (mid-morning). They divided by 4 for packaging (afternoon). They multiplied by 8 for batch stacking. They multiplied by 8 again (evening, using 'double' as word quantity, 'one distractor'). Time: morning/afternoon/evening. After first division and subtraction but before second division, how many units in the mid-morning?
